name: David Brown
opening_statement: I've had this nagging pain in my lower back for about 6 months now. It's really affecting my work as a warehouse supervisor.
emotional_baseline: Frustrated and concerned about work capacity, slightly anxious about potential serious pathology

symptoms.description: Lower back pain, worse with prolonged standing and lifting
symptoms.character: Dull ache, occasionally sharp with movement
symptoms.radiation: Occasional radiation to right buttock, no leg pain below knee
symptoms.timing: Worse at end of workday, improves with rest

rag_citation.guideline: Chronic non-specific low back pain typically presents with pain lasting >3 months, mechanical pattern, no neurological deficits
rag_citation.recommendation: Conservative management with activity modification, analgesia, and physiotherapy

rag_citation.source: eTG Musculoskeletal - Assessment of Back Pain
rag_citation.guideline: Morning stiffness <30 minutes suggests mechanical rather than inflammatory cause

symptoms.pattern: Wakes 2-3 times per night when rolling over

rag_citation.guideline: Sleep disturbance common in chronic pain, consider multimodal approach including sleep hygiene
rag_citation.recommendation: Address sleep quality as part of comprehensive pain management

symptoms.details: No fever, no weight loss, no bowel/bladder disturbance, no progressive neurological deficit, no saddle anaesthesia
symptoms.significance: Excludes serious pathology requiring urgent investigation

past_medical_history.management: Perindopril 5mg daily, BP controlled (135/85 mmHg average)

past_medical_history.details: BMI 32 kg/m², weight 98 kg, height 175 cm
past_medical_history.attempts: Multiple failed diet attempts, no formal weight management program

past_medical_history.outcome: Resolved with conservative management, returned to full work duties

family_history: Father had coronary artery disease (MI at age 62), mother has osteoarthritis. Two siblings alive and well. No family history of inflammatory arthritis or cancer.

social_history.occupation: Warehouse supervisor - requires prolonged standing, occasional heavy lifting
social_history.work_impact: Taking regular breaks, concerned about job security, reduced productivity
social_history.smoking: Ex-smoker, quit 5 years ago (20 pack-year history)
social_history.alcohol: 10-15 standard drinks per week, mostly weekends
social_history.exercise: Previously walked 30 minutes 3x/week, ceased 4 months ago due to pain
social_history.living_situation: Married, lives with wife in single-story home, two adult children
social_history.support: Good family support, wife accompanies to some appointments
social_history.functional_impact: Difficulty with prolonged driving, gardening, playing with grandchildren

examination_findings.general: Well-appearing male, comfortable at rest, no acute distress

spine.inspection: Normal lumbar lordosis, no visible deformity or asymmetry
spine.palpation: Tenderness over L4-L5 paraspinal muscles bilaterally, no midline tenderness
spine.range_of_motion: Flexion 60° (reduced from normal 80°), extension 15° (reduced from 25°), lateral flexion reduced bilaterally

special_tests.straight_leg_raise: Negative bilaterally (pain at 75°, no radicular symptoms)

lower_limbs.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick L2-S1 dermatomes

neurological.red_flags: No saddle anaesthesia, no bowel/bladder dysfunction

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, peripheral pulses intact
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze
examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, no masses, no AAA palpable

lumbar_spine_xray.rationale: Not indicated in first 6 weeks unless red flags present (eTG guideline)
lumbar_spine_xray.consider_if: No improvement after 6 weeks conservative management

mri_lumbar_spine.rationale: Reserve for suspected serious pathology or persistent radicular symptoms
mri_lumbar_spine.previous_study: 2020 MRI showed L5-S1 disc bulge, clinically resolved

blood_tests.fbc: Not routinely indicated unless systemic symptoms
blood_tests.esr_crp: Consider if suspected inflammatory cause (age <45, prolonged morning stiffness)
blood_tests.hba1c: Due for routine monitoring (last 3 months ago: 7.2%)

functional_assessment.pain_scale: VAS or numerical rating scale at each visit

actions: Reassure no serious pathology (no red flags)
Explain natural history: most chronic low back pain improves with conservative management
Emphasize importance of staying active despite pain
Advise against prolonged bed rest
Physiotherapy referral (MBS Item 10960 - GP Management Plan)
Encourage graded return to physical activity
Heat therapy for short-term symptom relief
Weight loss program referral (address BMI 32)
Ergonomic workplace assessment
Continue short-term NSAIDs (ibuprofen) with gastroprotection if prolonged use
Consider adding PPI (e.g., pantoprazole) given NSAID use
Discuss limited evidence for paracetamol (may cease if no benefit)
Avoid opioids for chronic non-specific low back pain (eTG recommendation)
Consider short-term muscle relaxant if severe muscle spasm (e.g., diazepam 2-5mg nocte, max 2 weeks)
pbs_items: Pantoprazole 20mg - PBS listed for NSAID gastroprotection
expected_management.medications_to_avoid: Opioids (tramadol, codeine combinations) - not recommended first-line

actions: Optimize diabetes control (current HbA1c 7.2%, target <7%)
Reinforce cardiovascular risk reduction (smoking cessation achieved, reduce alcohol)
Monitor blood pressure (currently 138/86, aim <130/80)
Annual diabetic complications screening
Review in 4-6 weeks to assess response to conservative management
Consider imaging (lumbar spine X-ray ± MRI) if no improvement at 6 weeks
Refer to specialist (orthopaedics or pain clinic) if refractory to conservative measures
Screen for depression/anxiety if pain becomes chronic (>3 months)
expected_management.red_flag_monitoring: Advise patient to return immediately if develops: progressive weakness, saddle anaesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, fever, unexplained weight loss

critical_errors.error: Ordering lumbar spine imaging (X-ray or MRI) in first 6 weeks without red flags
critical_errors.rationale: eTG guideline: imaging not indicated in first 6 weeks of non-specific low back pain unless red flags present. Over-investigation increases healthcare costs and may lead to unnecessary interventions for incidental findings.
critical_errors.correct_approach: Reassure patient, trial conservative management for 6 weeks before considering imaging

critical_errors.error: Prescribing opioids (tramadol, codeine combinations) as first-line analgesia
critical_errors.rationale: eTG explicitly recommends against opioids for chronic non-specific low back pain due to limited efficacy and significant harm (dependency, tolerance, adverse effects). This is an auto-fail error.
critical_errors.correct_approach: Use NSAIDs short-term with gastroprotection, consider muscle relaxants if severe spasm, refer to physiotherapy

critical_errors.rationale: eTG guideline: bed rest delays recovery and is associated with worse outcomes. Patients should be encouraged to remain as active as tolerable.
critical_errors.correct_approach: Advise staying active, modify activities as needed, graded return to normal function

critical_errors.error: Failing to address cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, obesity, ex-smoker)
critical_errors.rationale: Patient has multiple cardiovascular risk factors requiring ongoing management. Focusing solely on back pain without addressing comorbidities represents suboptimal holistic care.
critical_errors.correct_approach: Comprehensive management plan addressing HbA1c optimization, BP control, weight loss, alcohol reduction

critical_errors.error: Not assessing functional impact or red flags
critical_errors.rationale: Failure to screen for red flags (cauda equina, infection, malignancy, fracture) and assess functional disability is dangerous and represents inadequate assessment.
critical_errors.correct_approach: Systematically screen for red flags, quantify functional impact (Oswestry Disability Index), document neurological examination

critical_errors.error: Prescribing NSAIDs long-term without gastroprotection or renal monitoring
critical_errors.rationale: Patient on ACE inhibitor (perindopril) and has diabetes - at increased risk of NSAID-induced renal impairment. Long-term NSAID use requires PPI and renal function monitoring.
critical_errors.correct_approach: If NSAIDs required >2 weeks, add PPI, monitor renal function, review necessity regularly

fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent case for AMC Clinical Exam preparation. Appropriately represents chronic non-specific low back pain with realistic comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, obesity). Critical errors correctly identify common pitfalls: over-investigation, opioid prescribing, and inadequate red flag screening. eTG citations are accurate and relevant. Difficulty calibrated appropriately for medium level - requires management of multiple comorbidities and time-critical decision-making around imaging and specialist referral.
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: None - case is clinically accurate and educationally robust.

fracp_reviews.comments: Well-constructed case that tests key competencies: differentiating mechanical from inflammatory back pain, appropriate use of investigations, evidence-based conservative management, and holistic care. The inclusion of previous L5-S1 disc bulge (2020) adds realism and tests candidate's ability to interpret past imaging in current context. Social history appropriately highlights occupational factors and functional impact. FRACP-level case suitable for AMC Clinical Examination.
fracp_reviews.suggested_improvements: Consider adding brief mention of yellow flags (psychosocial factors predicting chronicity) in learning objectives, though current case is already comprehensive.

learning_objectives.objective: Differentiate mechanical (non-specific) low back pain from red flag conditions requiring urgent investigation
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Critical for patient safety - missing cauda equina, malignancy, or infection can have catastrophic outcomes
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Clinical assessment and diagnosis - musculoskeletal system

learning_objectives.objective: Apply evidence-based guidelines (eTG) for imaging in low back pain - avoid over-investigation
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Inappropriate early imaging increases healthcare costs, exposes patients to radiation, and often identifies incidental findings requiring unnecessary intervention
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Investigations and procedures - appropriate use of diagnostic tests

learning_objectives.objective: Prescribe analgesia safely in chronic pain - recognize opioid harms and alternatives
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Opioid crisis awareness - eTG explicitly recommends against opioids for chronic non-specific low back pain due to limited benefit and significant harm
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Therapeutics - safe prescribing and harm minimization

learning_objectives.objective: Manage comorbidities holistically - diabetes, hypertension, obesity in context of musculoskeletal complaint
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: General practice requires simultaneous management of multiple chronic conditions - not siloed organ-based care
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Chronic disease management and preventive care

learning_objectives.objective: Utilize multidisciplinary approach - physiotherapy referral, GP Management Plan (MBS 10960), Team Care Arrangement
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Complex chronic conditions benefit from coordinated care involving allied health professionals. Knowledge of MBS items demonstrates understanding of Australian healthcare system
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Health systems and practice management - use of Medicare items and allied health

learning_objectives.objective: Assess functional impact and occupational factors in chronic pain
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Chronic pain affects work capacity, relationships, mental health - comprehensive assessment includes functional disability (Oswestry Index) and psychosocial factors
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Biopsychosocial model of disease - considering patient's social context

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize when conservative management has failed and specialist referral is indicated
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: GPs must know their limitations - refractory pain (>6 weeks conservative management), progressive neurological deficit, or diagnostic uncertainty warrant specialist input
learning_objectives.amc_blueprint_alignment: Clinical decision-making - appropriate referral and escalation of care

learning_objectives.objective: Counsel patients on prognosis and self-management strategies for chronic pain
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Patient education and realistic expectation-setting are therapeutic interventions in themselves - most chronic low back pain improves with conservative measures and staying active
